headline: On-Device AI is now real, running offline for free on your phone
summary: Apple and Google's latest AI models are shifting from cloud-based to on-device processing, enabling offline, private, and cost-free AI agents.
details: The era of cloud-dependent AI is rapidly fading as major tech players like Apple and Google shift towards powerful on-device models. These new AI systems, exemplified by Apple's third-generation Foundation Models and Google's Gemma 4 family, are no longer scaled-down versions of their cloud counterparts. Instead, they are designed to run efficiently on personal hardware, offering significant advantages in cost, privacy, and accessibility.

A key shift is the elimination of per-token costs associated with cloud AI. Running AI models locally means the marginal cost of inference drops to approximately zero. This is a game-changer for agentic workloads, which can involve dozens of model calls for a single task. On-device AI makes complex, iterative tasks feasible without incurring escalating bills, fundamentally altering which AI-powered features are economically viable.

Beyond cost savings, on-device AI offers unparalleled privacy and offline functionality. Data processed locally never leaves the user's device, providing a stronger privacy guarantee than any cloud-based policy. Furthermore, these models function seamlessly on airplanes, in tunnels, or in regions with limited network connectivity, ensuring AI capabilities are always available.

The breakthrough isn't about cramming massive models into limited mobile RAM. Instead, it's a fundamental change in model architecture. Apple's Instruction-Following Pruning (IFP) and Google's Per-Layer Embeddings and Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) approaches allow models to store billions of parameters while activating only a few billion at any given time. This selective activation is key to fitting powerful AI into mobile hardware.

Modern neural processing units (NPUs) in smartphones and laptops are now capable of running these efficient on-device models at practical speeds. This hardware-software synergy has transformed the question from 'can it run?' to 'which model fits this RAM tier?', a standard product development challenge rather than a research hurdle. This enables features like real-time background summarization or complex agent loops that were previously impractical.

The capability jump is particularly evident in multimodality. Apple's AFM 3 on-device model now processes images, with human raters preferring its understanding over 60% of the time compared to the previous generation. This advancement promises more sophisticated and integrated AI experiences directly on user devices.
